title: A Better Understanding of Flexoelectric and Ferroelectric Displacements from Electron Ptychography of Both the Anion and Cation Sublattices
content: A common approximation in electron microscopy studies of ferroelectric materials is to infer the ionic polarization of a material solely from the measurement of cation-cation displacements. This is necessitated by the inability of traditional atomic-resolution microscopy methods to reliably detect or locate light atoms such as oxygen in the presence of much heavier cations. However, measuring only cation-cation displacements overlooks the essence of a dipole moment, which requires an offset between the cations and anions. For the sub-class of perovskite-derived displacive ferroelectrics, this cation-only approach using high-angle annular dark field (HAADF) imaging has provided useful qualitative maps, even though the magnitude and sometimes even the sign of the displacements can be wrong when octahedral tilts occur [1]. An early application of aberration-corrected transmission electron microscopy (TEM) was imaging the oxygen sublattice in perovskite ferroelectrics, although the sample thickness was limited by multiple scattering to under 6nm, where surface relaxations can still be quite significant. More recent work with differential phase contrast has also proved sensitive to the oxygen sublattice, but quantitative analysis is confounded by extreme sensitivity to sample tilt and thickness variations as well.
